# Cartoon Explainer Video (default video style)

Generate a narrated **flat-cartoon storytime explainer** MP4 — the studio's default
look. edge-tts (or a supplied audio file) provides the voiceover + per-word timings,
then Remotion renders one animated "beat" per script paragraph in a light,
playful, TheOdd1sOut-inspired style.

**Project root:** `C:\Users\nmalipeddy\source\repos\Learn\whiteboard-studio`
Always run commands from that folder. Composition id: **`Cartoon`**.

## When to use
This is the **default** for any "make me a video / short / reel / explainer /
animation" request. Only use another skill/composition if the user explicitly asks
for that style (e.g. "whiteboard", "handwriting").

## Full delivery package (DEFAULT whenever the user gives a script)
When the user pastes a script, deliver ALL of these without being asked, using a
short slug for file names (e.g. `speed-india`, `kashmir`, `hyd-vs-blr`):

| # | Deliverable | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Video (vertical 1080x1920 unless told otherwise) | `out/<slug>.mp4` |
| 2 | Clickbait 9:16 thumbnail | `out/<slug>-thumbnail-9x16.png` |
| 3 | Telugu subtitle track, synced to the narration | `out/<slug>.te.srt` |
| 4 | YouTube upload package (titles, description with chapters, tags, thumbnail concepts, pinned comment, settings) | in the chat reply |

Workflow:
1. Save the script as `<slug>-script.txt`, one beat per paragraph. Remove emoji and
   markdown (`**`) from the spoken text.
2. Pick the right visual for each beat: **every beat must fill the screen**. Don't
   leave a character alone on an empty background. Use a `compare` VS card, a
   `route` map, a map card, a chart, logos, or a dedicated composition.
3. Author `public/beats.json` (same count and order as the paragraphs). If you
   overwrite another video's beats, save them first as `public/beats.<slug>.json`.
4. Run `node generate.mjs --file <slug>-script.txt --voice <voice> --size vertical --comp <Comp> --out out/<slug>.mp4`.
   Before the full render, check 2-3 stills with `view_image`.
5. Make the thumbnail: copy an existing `*ThumbnailV.tsx`, register it in
   `src/Root.tsx`, then `npx remotion still src/index.ts <Id> out/<slug>-thumbnail-9x16.png --frame=0 --overwrite`
   and check it with `view_image`. Fix any overlapping text.
6. Make the Telugu SRT: print the section times with
   `node -e "const t=require('./public/timing.json');t.sections.forEach((s,i)=>console.log(i,s.start.toFixed(2),s.end.toFixed(2),s.text.slice(0,30)))"`
   and write one cue per section, or split long sections (over ~8s) into 2 cues.
   Use natural Telugu. Keep proper nouns and acronyms recognisable (LoC, BrahMos, IT).
   Timestamps use the `HH:MM:SS,mmm` format.
7. Write the YouTube package by following the **youtube-upload-package** skill.
   Set the chapter timestamps from `timing.json` section starts. If the video is
   over 60s, point out that it won't get the Shorts shelf unless it's trimmed.
8. Open the video (`Invoke-Item out/<slug>.mp4`) and list every output path.

## India map rules (IMPORTANT)
- Always use the **official Indian boundary**, which includes PoK/PoJK,
  Gilgit-Baltistan and Aksai Chin. `src/india/geo/IND.json` is already that outline
  (generated by `pipeline/simplify_india.mjs` from datameet `india-composite.geojson`).
  Never swap in an international/UN-view India polygon.
- Draw India **after** Pakistan and China so its fill covers the disputed areas.
- Map regions must reach `latMax >= 37.8` so the northern tip isn't cut off.
- For disputed-territory topics, colour each zone by the country that
  **administers** it, state India's claim in the text, show a legend, and ground
  the zones on the India outline with a full-India locator inset (see `Kashmir`).

## The look (already built)
Each beat renders on a pastel background with:
- **Section pill** (top-left), optional **date/chapter pill**
- **Big rounded title** (Baloo font — supports Telugu + Latin)
- **Storytime character(s)** — rounded avatar with expressions
  (`happy | surprised | worried | annoyed | neutral`), blink, gestures, **crowds**,
  and **lip-sync** driven by the narration's word timings
- **Gray caption**, **button**, **big arrow**
- Optional **map card** (light card, thick outlines) for geography topics
- Optional **company logo row** (real brand glyphs) and a **3D bar chart** (WebGL)
- **Sound effects** auto-played per beat (whoosh / ding / pop / riser / boom)

## How to make one (steps)

1. **Write the script** → save to a file (e.g. `my-script.txt`), **one beat per
   paragraph**, separated by blank lines. Keep each paragraph short and spoken.
   Match the user's language. This is what the voice reads.

2. **Author the beats** → `public/beats.json` is an **array with one object per
   paragraph** (same count/order as the script). Each beat:
   ```jsonc
   {
     "bg": "#ffe0c2",              // pastel background for this beat
     "label": "HOOK",              // top-left section pill
     "datePill": "2022",           // optional dark pill
     "title": "BIG TITLE",         // optional bold title
     "titleColor": "#c1121f",      // optional
     "big": true,                  // optional: huge title + pop-lines
     "caption": "small gray line",  // optional
     "button": "FOLLOW",           // optional rounded button
     "buttonColor": "#3b6bff",      // optional
     "arrow": true,                 // optional big arrow
     "chars": { "expr": "happy", "skin": "#ffffff", "label": "NAME", "count": 1 },
     "logos": ["oracle", "amazon", "dell", "meta", "microsoft"], // optional brand logo row
     "chart": "layoffs",           // optional 3D bar chart (see Chart3D data)
     "sfx": "boom",                // optional: pop | whoosh | ding | riser | boom
     "map": "intro",                // optional: "intro" | "crimea" | "invasion" | "india"
     "route": "car",                // optional: vehicle drives Kashmir -> Kanyakumari on the India map
                                    //   car | train | plane | jet | rocket (faster ones launch harder)
     "icon": "jet",                 // optional: big static vehicle icon
     "compare": {                   // optional: FULL-SCREEN head-to-head VS card
       "metric": "Population", "unit": "sq km", "note": "verdict line",
       "winner": "left",           // crown on the winner (left | right)
       "left":  { "name": "BENGALURU", "value": 14, "display": "14 M", "sub": "...", "items": ["Swiggy"], "color": "#e63946" },
       "right": { "name": "HYDERABAD", "value": 11.3, "display": "11.3 M", "color": "#3b6bff" }
     }
   }
   ```
   Which visual to use: `compare` for any "A vs B" script, `route` for travel or
   distance scripts, a map for geography, `chart` for rankings, and `logos` for
   companies.
   Guidance: vary `bg` per section for rhythm; use `big:true` for punchlines;
   give two characters different `skin`/`label` for dialogue; use `count>1` for
   crowds; only use `map` for Russia/Ukraine geography (other topics: omit it).
   Keep on-screen `title`/`caption` short — the full sentence is spoken, not shown.
   SFX default to `whoosh` (or `boom` on `big` beats); a `ding` also fires on
   `logos`/`chart` reveals — set `sfx` to override.

3. **Pick voice / size** from the user's intent:
   - Telugu `te-IN-MohanNeural` (M) / `te-IN-ShrutiNeural` (F),
     Hindi `hi-IN-MadhurNeural`, Indian-English `en-IN-PrabhatNeural`,
     US-English `en-US-AndrewNeural`. List all: `python -m edge_tts --list-voices`.
   - Shorts/Reels → `vertical`; YouTube → `landscape`.

4. **Generate + render:**
   ```powershell
   node generate.mjs --file my-script.txt --voice te-IN-MohanNeural --size vertical --comp Cartoon --out out/video.mp4
   ```
   (`generate.mjs` runs edge-tts → timings → typecheck → Remotion render of the
   `Cartoon` composition. It's the beats in `public/beats.json` + timings in
   `public/timing.json` that drive the visuals.)

5. **Verify before the full render** (recommended for long videos): render a few
   stills first, e.g.
   `npx remotion still src/index.ts Cartoon out/chk.png --frame=40 --overwrite`,
   view them, adjust `beats.json`, then render.

6. **Report** the output path to the user.

## Using the user's own recorded voiceover (no TTS)
```powershell
node pipeline/use_audio.mjs "C:\path\to\voice.m4a" my-script.txt
npx remotion render src/index.ts Cartoon out/video.mp4 --overwrite
```
`use_audio.mjs` converts the audio to `public/audio.mp3` and writes
`public/timing.json` with one section per paragraph (length ≈ paragraph length).
Scene sync is approximate; nudge paragraph splits if a beat drifts.

## Extras — logos, 3D charts, sound effects
- **Company logos:** add `"logos": [slug, ...]` to a beat. Real glyphs for
  dell/meta/paypal/adidas are baked in `src/cartoon/logos.ts`; microsoft/oracle/
  amazon are hand-drawn in `src/cartoon/LogoRow.tsx`. Add more brands by extracting
  from the `simple-icons` npm package (regenerate via `pipeline/gen_logos.mjs`).
- **3D bar chart:** add `"chart": "layoffs"` (real WebGL via `@remotion/three`).
  Edit the data array in `src/cartoon/Chart3D.tsx`. Requires
  `Config.setChromiumOpenGlRenderer("angle")` in `remotion.config.ts` (already set).
- **Sound effects:** WAVs live in `public/sfx/` (self-synthesized, royalty-free).
  Regenerate/tune them with `node pipeline/gen_sfx.mjs`. Each beat auto-plays one;
  set `"sfx"` per beat to choose. Kept at low volume so narration stays clear.

## Thumbnails (cartoon theme)
Still compositions render a matching thumbnail:
```powershell
npx remotion still src/index.ts Thumbnail  out/thumb-16x9.png --frame=0 --overwrite   # 1280x720
npx remotion still src/index.ts ThumbnailV out/thumb-9x16.png --frame=0 --overwrite   # 1080x1920
```
Edit `src/cartoon/Thumbnail.tsx` / `ThumbnailV.tsx` (title, banner, logos, character)
per video. Map-based videos have their own (e.g. `IndiaThumbnailV`).

## Subtitle tracks (any language)
Author short caption lines per section in a cues JSON (one array per paragraph),
then build a timed `.srt` from `public/timing.json`:
```powershell
node pipeline/make_srt.mjs my.cues.json out/subs.srt
```
Upload on YouTube via Subtitles → Add language → Upload file (with timing).

## Voice tuning
`config.json` holds `voice`, `rate` (e.g. `"+5%"`), `pitch` (e.g. `"+0Hz"`).
`generate.mjs` accepts `--voice` and `--rate`; pitch is read from `config.json`.

## Country-map videos
For geography topics with many countries, use the dedicated `IndiaBorders`
composition (`src/india/`) as the pattern: it loads per-country GeoJSON
(`src/india/geo/`), highlights a focus country per beat, shows km badges, and ends
with a 3D bar chart (`src/india/BorderChart3D.tsx`). Copy this module for other
regions by swapping the GeoJSON + data.

For disputed or sub-national regions, use `Kashmir` (`src/kashmir/`) as the pattern.
`zones.ts` holds schematic zone polygons, each tagged with its administering
country and colour, plus LoC/LAC polylines. `KashmirExplainer.tsx` keeps its beats
inside the file, focuses different zones per beat, and draws the India base map
with a locator inset and a legend. `MapView` accepts `lines` (dashed borders) and
`movers` (animated icons).

## First-time setup (only if it fails on a fresh machine)
```powershell
npm install
python -m pip install edge-tts
```
A Chromium (Chrome/Edge) is required; `remotion.config.ts` auto-detects one. To
force it, set `"browserExecutable"` in `config.json`.

## Troubleshooting
- **Beats/scenes out of sync with narration** — `beats.json` must have the **same
  number of entries (and order)** as the script's paragraphs.
- **Telugu/Hindi text shows boxes** — use the Baloo/Noto fonts already wired in
  `src/story/fonts.ts`; don't switch captions to a Latin-only font.
- **Emoji show as tofu** — headless Chrome lacks color-emoji; use drawn elements
  or expressions instead of emoji in on-screen text.
- **Text overflows** — shorten the `title`/`caption`; they're meant to be punchy.
